- the domain of [MATH: f(x)] is [MATH: [1,2],] and
- the range of [MATH: f(x)] is [MATH: [2,6].]

Content:
Recall that each point [MATH: (a,b)] on the graph of [MATH: {\color{blue}y=f(x)}] has a corresponding point [MATH: (b,a)] on the graph of the inverse function [MATH: {\color{red}y=f^{-1}(x)}.] That is to say, the [MATH: x] and [MATH: y] coordinates swap.

Content:

- the range of [MATH: f^{-1}(x)] is [MATH: [1,2].]

Content:
In general:

Content:
- The domain of a function [MATH: {\color{blue}f(x)}] is the range of its inverse function [MATH: {\color{red}f^{-1}(x)}.]
- The range of a function [MATH: {\color{blue}f(x)}] is the domain of its inverse function [MATH: {\color{red}f^{-1}(x)}.]
